purpose: Demonstration that the generated X01_SOURCE_INTEGRITY gate result is invariant to the presence or absence of the source bytes it claims to verify.
note: Timestamps are deliberately omitted: this package must be byte-reproducible. Ordering is established by git history.
affectedClaim: X01_SOURCE_INTEGRITY reports PASS in the generated cross-study report.
mechanism: scripts/run-cross-study-parity.py:360-363 computes X01 from all(item['verified']) and cacheVerification['status']=='PASS' — JSON literals read out of the corpus file the gate is meant to validate. It performs zero filesystem reads of the artefacts.

experiment.state: cache FULL (12 artifacts, 75001736 bytes, every SHA-256 independently verified)

prediction: The generated report would be byte-identical with and without the cache, and X01 would report PASS in both states.
observed: CONFIRMED. Byte-identical report SHA-256 in both states; X01 PASS in both.
correctionToEarlierProse: X01 is vacuous AS A GENERATED REPORT GATE. This is narrower than 'no source verification exists anywhere'. tests/cross-study-parity.test.mjs CAN hash real source files when they are present; its weakness is that line 39 wraps the hashing in fs.existsSync and line 45 explicitly accepts checkedArtifacts === 0. The two mechanisms are distinct and both statements must be carried.

statusVocabularyDefect.consequence: CLAUDE.md:119-121 requires an absent dataset to be marked BLOCKED / NOT RUN / EXTERNAL VALIDATION REQUIRED. That status is currently unrepresentable, and no schema or validator constrains status strings, so a typo would render unstyled and fail no test.

uncertainty: Corrupted-cache and substituted-cache states were NOT tested in Phase A. They are specified in red test C2.
alternativeExplanation: None surviving: byte-identity of the report under a 75 MB change in filesystem state admits no alternative reading.
